beats.care: Planning a US master's? Fewer students may get to work after graduating, which makes that loan harder to repay.
beats.what: The US proposed making colleges pay $70,000 for each international student who wants to work there after graduating.
beats.why: The US government says its OPT work programme is misused to hire cheaper foreign workers.

cards.body: On 7 Oct, the US government (Department of Homeland Security) proposed a new rule: colleges must pay $70,000 for each international student they recommend for OPT, plus $30,000 for each extension.
If the fee isn't paid, the student doesn't get permission to work.
cards.caption: roughly what $70,000 is in rupees

cards.body: OPT lets foreign students work in the US in their field after they graduate: usually 1 year, and up to 3 years for STEM students. For lots of Indian students, that job is how they pay back their education loan.
cards.title: wait, what is OPT?

cards.body: Breathe: it's a *proposal*, not a law yet. People can send comments first, and colleges or companies may take it to court. But if it passes, the government itself expects colleges to recommend far fewer students.

a.body: OPT gets misused and has become a way to hire cheaper foreign workers instead of Americans.
a.label: The US government says

b.body: OPT fills skill gaps in tech and science, and it's a big reason students choose the US at all.
b.label: Colleges & student groups say
